title: What Learning Cities Is
definition: Learning Cities: cities where every block teaches something.
description:
Learning Cities — Signature Edition: cities where every block teaches something. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature campus hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: school districts rethought, study transit rebuilt, open curricula reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the library blocks ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Learning Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Learning Cities.
description:
The Signature vision of Learning Cities does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature campus hulls program, charter one: master school districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale study transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate open curricula systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Learning Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: The campus hulls Grid
definition: The campus hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Learning Cities.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one school districts grid that the campus hulls district runs on.

In the Learning Cities architecture, the campus hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the campus hulls fails outright — Learning Cities stops being Learning Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

t: 2030 — The first campus hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first campus hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Learning Cities roadmap.
description:
The first campus hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its school districts grid and study transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the school districts results have to replicate outside the lab, study transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and open curricula operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed school districts demonstrations, study transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting open curricula uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)
key_points: Target year: 2030 (4 years out).
Depends on: school districts, study transit, open curricula.

title: Readiness Estimator: Learning Cities
definition: Estimates Learning Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Learning Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a campus hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Learning Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Learning Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Learning Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 90538 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where school districts monitoring, study transit redundancy, or open curricula maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Learning Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Learning Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Learning Cities — cities where every block teaches something.

Phase 1 — Prove (school districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (study transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (open curricula): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (library blocks): campus hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and urban core-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
key_points: Four phases: Prove, Build, Operate, Compound.
Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
